summary: Interactions API: the presence_penalty and frequency_penalty generation options and the cached_content request/response field are removed (no longer supported)
The Interactions namespace no longer exports the Arguments type (URL context call arguments; use URLContextCallArguments) or the RetrievalType type

models.generateImages() and models.editImage() (Imagen) and models.generateVideos() called with prompt/image/video arguments now log deprecation warnings (removal planned for a future major; use generateContent with image models, or the source argument)
HttpOptions.timeout now bounds each HTTP attempt (each retry gets a fresh deadline) instead of the whole call
response_modalities on Interactions create params (CreateModelInteraction/CreateAgentInteraction) and on Interaction is marked @deprecated
The StreamMetadata type and the metadata (total_usage) field are removed from Interactions stream events (interaction.created/completed, status updates, step start/stop)
The deprecated Interactions Turn and TurnContent types are removed from the exported types
The call_id field is removed from the Interactions FunctionResultDelta stream type
The Interactions environment network Allowlist type changes from an object { allowlist?: AllowlistEntry[] } to AllowlistEntry[] | 'disabled'

On Node, requests made without an explicit timeout are no longer cut off by undici's default headers/body timeouts (the SDK's default HTTP timeouts are raised so long-running calls are not killed client-side)
The minimum supported TypeScript version is raised to 5.6 (from 5.4 after 2.12.0); older TypeScript versions are no longer tested

QueryClient's fetchQuery, prefetchQuery, ensureQueryData, fetchInfiniteQuery, prefetchInfiniteQuery and ensureInfiniteQueryData (and the FetchQueryOptions/EnsureQueryDataOptions/EnsureInfiniteQueryDataOptions types) are deprecated in favor of the new queryClient.query() / queryClient.infiniteQuery() (with staleTime: 'static' for the ensure* variants)
The experimental_prefetchInRender QueryClient/query option and the promise property on useQuery/useInfiniteQuery results (for use with React use()) are removed

usePrefetchQuery and usePrefetchInfiniteQuery now run through queryClient.query()/infiniteQuery() instead of prefetchQuery()/prefetchInfiniteQuery(), so they honor enabled: false, skipToken and select (no fetch when disabled) where they used to fetch regardless

The TData type parameter of UseInfiniteQueryOptions and UseSuspenseInfiniteQueryOptions now defaults to InfiniteData<TQueryFnData> instead of TQueryFnData, so options typed with the defaults describe the paginated shape

hydrate()/HydrationBoundary no longer fall back for dehydrated queries without dehydratedAt (now a required field of the dehydrated query type): such entries no longer count as newer data or get dataUpdatedAt = now, and their pending promises are not picked up
`Astro.cookies.set()` no longer percent-encodes cookie values made only of URL-safe characters in `Set-Cookie` (cookie v2); other encoded values round-trip as before.
The undocumented `app.pipeline` property and the `AppPipeline` export from `astro/app` are removed; adapters should call the new `app.getLogger()` instead of `app.pipeline.getLogger()`.

The content data store now rebuilds module imports from `deferredRender` entries on every write, so an import added only via `addModuleImport()` without a matching `deferredRender` entry is no longer preserved across writes.
Astro's optional `sharp` dependency range moves from `^0.34.0 || ^0.35.0` to `^0.35.4`, dropping support for sharp 0.34.

In MDX, a dynamic expression passed as a `<script>` or `<style>` child (e.g. `<script>{value}</script>`) is now escaped like other element content instead of rendered raw; use `set:html` to opt back into raw output.
`security.checkOrigin` is reimplemented after Go's CSRF protection and now also decides on the `Sec-Fetch-Site` header, not only `Origin`, when accepting or rejecting unsafe requests.
The minimum supported Node.js version is raised to 22.22.0.

Custom prerenderers (`setPrerenderer`) that return a plain array from `getStaticPaths()` or a plain `Response` from `render()` are deprecated; return `{ paths, metadata }` / result objects so images on prerendered pages are generated.
HttpStatusCode.PayloadTooLarge (413) is deprecated in favor of the new HttpStatusCode.ContentTooLarge
HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableEntity (422) is deprecated in favor of the new HttpStatusCode.UnprocessableContent
With the fetch adapter maxRedirects: 0 now prevents redirects from being followed (manual redirect mode, exposing the 3xx or an opaque redirect) instead of being ignored
NO_PROXY entries now accept IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR ranges, so 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 bypass the proxy for every destination where such entries previously matched nothing
data: URIs whose media type contains extra slash separators now reject with ERR_INVALID_URL instead of being parsed

A custom fetch implementation (env.fetch) now gets method, headers, body, signal, duplex and credentials only on the resolved Request (first argument); those fields are no longer on the second fetchOptions argument, where custom implementations used to read them
An explicit proxy config combined with httpVersion 2 now rejects with ERR_NOT_SUPPORT instead of being silently ignored (request sent directly)
Config fields inherited from an Object.create(null) template object (a config whose prototype is a null-prototype object) are now ignored, where they used to be honored
Interceptor manager replacement objects that need sanitizing are now stored as normalized null-prototype snapshots, losing their original identity, prototype, instanceof branding and accessors
Database joins leave `experimental`: `experimental: { joins: true }` is replaced by `advanced: { database: { joins: true } }` (default false)
The account table gains a required `issuer` column, and accounts are keyed on (issuer, accountId) instead of (providerId, accountId); 1.7.3 reverted this to (providerId, accountId) with no issuer

getAccessToken, refreshToken, accountInfo and unlinkAccount select an account by the local `account.id`, passed as `accountId`, or with `useAccountCookie: true`; `providerId` is removed from these selectors, and omitting both no longer falls back to the account cookie

The provider account id now comes from the raw verified profile (OIDC `sub`, plain OAuth `id`, or a new `accountSubject` option) with no runtime fallback; `mapProfileToUser` can no longer return `id`, `getUserInfo().user` no longer carries it, and `accountInfo` exposes it as `account.accountId` instead of `user.id`
The generic OAuth `microsoftEntraId` helper requires a concrete tenant GUID; `common`, `organizations` and `consumers` tenants are no longer accepted (use the built-in `microsoft` provider)
Microsoft accounts (built-in `microsoft` provider and the `microsoftEntraId` helper) are identified by the `oid` claim instead of `sub`, and tokens without a valid `oid` are rejected
The captcha plugin's `endpoints` entries must match full auth paths; partial prefixes such as `/sign-in` no longer cover `/sign-in/email` and need a wildcard (`/sign-in/*` or `/sign-in/**`)

The `mcp` plugin, `withMcpAuth`, `mcpHandler` and the in-core MCP client (`createMcpAuthClient`) are removed from `better-auth`; the plugin moves to `@better-auth/mcp` (`requireMcpAuth`, `createMcpProtectedRequestHandler`, flat options instead of `oidcConfig`, endpoints at /oauth2/* instead of /mcp/*)

OAuth provider access tokens bound to a session become inactive when the session ends: introspection returns `{ active: false }` and /oauth2/userinfo rejects them, where before they stayed valid until their TTL
The OAuth provider's `validAudiences` option is removed in favour of explicit `resources`; refresh tokens now use the shortest applicable TTL, and the `jwks` table gains `alg` and `crv` columns

SCIM provisioning no longer runs on the organization plugin: its configuration, client APIs, database schema and Group model are replaced, and existing state can't be migrated in place (full reprovision)
`enableTwoFactor` returns a discriminated response with a `method` field (`"totp"` with `totpURI` and `backupCodes`, or `"otp"`); callers must narrow on `method` before reading `totpURI`

With a dynamic `baseURL: { allowedHosts }`, the origin is resolved from `Host` and `x-forwarded-host`/`x-forwarded-proto` are ignored unless `advanced.trustedProxyHeaders: true`; requests with no usable or allowed host fail closed without `baseURL.fallback`
The device authorization plugin's `deviceCode` and `userCode` columns get unique indexes and a 191-character limit, so custom generators must return unique values of at most 191 characters
The device authorization `/device` endpoint gets a default rate limit of 5 requests per window equal to the code lifetime
Default-generated device user codes are now matched ignoring case and readability separators during verification, approval and denial (custom codes outside the default alphabet still match exactly)

The Electron sign-in flow requires S256 PKCE: the `code_challenge_method` parameter and the `disableOriginOverride` option are removed, plain PKCE is rejected, and the `electron-origin` header is no longer trusted

Custom-scheme `trustedOrigins` entries are matched by scheme and authority instead of string prefix, so a host-bearing entry like `myapp://callback` no longer matches `myapp://callback.attacker.tld` (host-less `myapp://` still matches any host)
The One Tap plugin refuses to verify ID tokens unless a Google client ID is configured via `oneTap({ clientId })` or `socialProviders.google.clientId`
Google One Tap binds accounts to the verified Google subject instead of matching existing users by email
The deprecated `oidcProvider` plugin is removed from `better-auth/plugins`; use `oauthProvider` from `@better-auth/oauth-provider`

Generic OAuth's dedicated client APIs are removed: `signIn.oauth2({ providerId })` becomes `signIn.social({ provider })`, `oauth2.link()` becomes `linkSocial()`, and the `genericOAuthClient()` client plugin is dropped
Generic OAuth providers use the shared callback route `/api/auth/callback/:id` instead of `/api/auth/oauth2/callback/:id`
Generic OAuth providers default `pkce` to true (was false); set `pkce: false` for providers that reject PKCE
Generic OAuth's `issuer` and `requireIssuerValidation` config options are removed; issuer validation comes from OIDC discovery
Generic OAuth's `authorizationUrlParams` and `tokenUrlParams` accept only `Record<string, string>`

Generic OAuth providers configured with `discoveryUrl` now verify the provider's id_token against its JWKS and bind it to a server-generated nonce, rejecting sign-ins that fail; set `disableIdTokenNonceBinding: true` for providers that don't echo the nonce

Custom `UpstreamProvider` implementations lose the `verifyIdToken` method; client-submitted id_tokens are checked by one shared verifier driven by an `idToken` config (JWKS, issuer, audience, or a `verify` function)
PayPal `signIn.social({ idToken })` now returns `ID_TOKEN_NOT_SUPPORTED` instead of accepting any decodable id_token; redirect sign-in is unchanged

`verifyAccessToken` from `better-auth/oauth2` (and the `oauthProviderResourceClient` action) is renamed `verifyBearerToken` and rejects DPoP-bound tokens; `AccessTokenRequestInput` is renamed `ResourceRequestInput`

The synchronous OAuth2 request builders `createAuthorizationCodeRequest`, `createRefreshAccessTokenRequest` and `createClientCredentialsTokenRequest` are removed; use the async `authorizationCodeRequest`, `refreshAccessTokenRequest` and `clientCredentialsTokenRequest`

SIWE nonces are issued before the wallet is known: `authClient.siwe.nonce()`/`getNonce()` no longer accept wallet address or chain ID, a server `getNonce` must return an ERC-4361 nonce (8–250 alphanumerics), and address and chain are read from the signed message
The public `generateState()` helper takes an options object, `generateState(c, options)`, instead of positional `(c, link, additionalData)` arguments
The OAuth callback redirect error code `email_doesn't_match` is renamed `email_does_not_match`
The public `getIp` helper export is renamed `getIP`
Custom `secondaryStorage` must implement `increment(key, ttl)` and `getAndDelete(key)`, which were optional before
Custom rate-limit storage must implement a single `consume(key, rule)` method; separate `get`/`set` storage is no longer accepted (in 1.6 `consume` was optional, with a fallback to get/set)
Magic-link and email-OTP sign-in to an account whose email was never verified now remove its unproven password and other linked accounts and revoke existing sessions before signing the user in

Signing out with `secondaryStorage` and `session.preserveSessionInDatabase` now runs `session.delete` hooks, marks the preserved session ended and revokes OAuth tokens bound to it; before, the hooks were skipped
The session cookie cache is tied to the `session_token` cookie, so cached session data is used only together with the matching session token
`organization.updateTeam` no longer accepts `id`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt` in the request body
`updateMemberRole` now validates that the role exists after the authorization checks rather than before, so an unauthorized caller gets the permission error first
A failed two-factor challenge cleanup returns the new error code `FAILED_TO_INVALIDATE_TWO_FACTOR_CHALLENGE`
Device authorization `/device/code` and `/device/token` responses (and OAuth credential responses) now send `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`

Built-in placeholder emails use `{identifier}@{namespace}.placeholder.invalid`, e.g. anonymous users get `{id}@anonymous.placeholder.invalid` and SIWE users `{wallet}@siwe.placeholder.invalid` (unless `emailDomainName` is set) instead of the old `temp@{id}.com`-, `.local`- or base-URL-domain formats
`getTestInstance` from `better-auth/test` uses a fast password hasher by default instead of the production hashing cost; a custom `emailAndPassword.password` still takes precedence

Better Auth validates the database schema at initialization by default, including in production, and rejects authentication requests while the schema doesn't match; opt out with `advanced.database.validateSchema: false`
The OAuth proxy plugin's legacy `/oauth-proxy-callback` endpoint is deprecated, to be removed in the next minor release

Passwords longer than `maxPasswordLength` are rejected with `PASSWORD_TOO_LONG` before hashing on sign-in (email, username, phone number), verify-password, change-password, delete-user, two-factor password endpoints and admin create-user, as sign-up and reset already did

Magic Link records and database-backed OAuth/SAML state are stored under separate verification identifier prefixes (`magic-link:`, `auth-state:`), and Magic Link verification accepts only Magic Link records; links issued before the upgrade stop working and `verification.storeIdentifier.overrides` rules must match the new prefixes

OAuth state cookies and OAuth Proxy payloads are encrypted with purpose-specific keys instead of the shared key, so sign-ins started before the upgrade and mixed old/new OAuth Proxy participants can't exchange state

.env.vault support is removed: config() no longer decrypts a .env.vault file when DOTENV_KEY is set (the DOTENV_KEY option, the DOTENV_KEY and DOTENV_CONFIG_DOTENV_KEY env vars and the DotenvConfigOptions.DOTENV_KEY type are gone; it always reads the plain .env), and the decrypt() export (plus _configVault/_parseVault) no longer exists

Preload configuration is removed in favour of the new dotenv run CLI: node -r dotenv/config no longer reads dotenv_config_<option>=value command-line arguments, and the dotenv/lib/env-options and dotenv/lib/cli-options subpath exports are gone; import 'dotenv/config' itself still works (but logged by default until 18.0.4, where 17.x preloads were quiet)
config()'s '◇ injected env (n) from .env' message is written to stderr (console.error) instead of stdout (console.log); debug lines stay on stdout
The random '// tip: …' suffix (dotenvx/vestauth promotions and option hints, present since 17.1.0) is dropped from the injection message, which now ends after the file list

DOTENV_CONFIG_PATH, DOTENV_CONFIG_ENCODING and DOTENV_CONFIG_OVERRIDE (and the new DOTENV_PATH/ENCODING/OVERRIDE/FAST names) now set defaults for every config() call, where before a direct config() call honoured only DOTENV_CONFIG_DEBUG and DOTENV_CONFIG_QUIET and the rest applied only through the dotenv/config preload

Options passed to config() now take precedence over DOTENV_* and DOTENV_CONFIG_* environment variables, where 17.2.0 documented the opposite (a DOTENV_CONFIG_* variable overrode code-set options such as {quiet: false})

import 'dotenv/config' (and node -r dotenv/config) defaults quiet to true again, so it prints no injection message unless DOTENV_QUIET=false or DOTENV_CONFIG_QUIET=false is set; 18.0.0 to 18.0.3 logged by default

populate()'s return type DotenvPopulateOutput declares its values as string | undefined instead of string, so under strict null checks a populated value must be narrowed before use as a string (a declaration correction; runtime unchanged)

radix now reports Number["parseInt"](...) calls written with computed member access that lack a radix, and calls whose radix is a signed numeric literal outside 2-36 such as -1 or +37; before, both were left unreported.
no-loss-of-precision now reports nonzero numeric literals that underflow to 0 or -0 (such as 1e-350 or -1e-350); before, any literal whose value was 0 was skipped.
no-unexpected-multiline now treats a division on a new line followed by d or v (regex flag letters) as a possible regex literal and reports it, as it already did for g, i, m, s, u and y.

new-cap no longer exempts lowercase names that happen to be Object.prototype properties (new hasOwnProperty(), new toString() and the like) from newIsCap, because the exception lists are now Sets instead of plain-object lookups; such calls are now reported unless listed in newIsCapExceptions.

no-extra-bind now reports .bind(this) on a function whose only uses of this are inside class field initializers or static blocks (where this does not refer to the function), which it previously left unreported.
no-unsafe-finally (in eslint:recommended) now reports a labeled continue inside a finally block that jumps to a loop outside the try statement; before, labeled continue was not checked.

new-cap capIsNew no longer exempts the built-in constructor names (Array, Boolean, Date, Error, Function, Number, Object, RegExp, String, Symbol, BigInt) everywhere: they are exempt only when they refer to the global (directly or via globalThis, window, self, global), so calling a local, imported or shadowed Date(...) or Number(...) without new is now reported.
object-shorthand with ignoreConstructors: true now also ignores constructor-like (capitalized) quoted property names such as "Foo": function () {}; before, quoted keys were still reported.

new-cap reads the first Unicode code point of a name instead of the first UTF-16 code unit, so identifiers starting with an astral uppercase or lowercase letter are now classified and reported like other capitalized or lowercase names.

no-use-before-define with variables: false or classes: false now reports references inside immediately invoked (non-generator, non-suspending) functions to variables or classes declared later, since the IIFE runs before they are initialized; before, such references were exempt as being in a separate function scope.

no-obj-calls (in eslint:recommended) now reports calling or constructing globalThis itself (globalThis(), new globalThis(), including through aliases), in addition to Math, JSON, Reflect, Atomics and Intl.
no-unsafe-optional-chaining (in eslint:recommended) now reports yield* with an optional-chain argument that can short-circuit to undefined (yield* obj?.items), which it did not check before.
req.fresh (and so res.send's 304 handling) now evaluates conditional-request validators for QUERY requests as well as GET/HEAD; a QUERY with a matching ETag previously always got the full response
The HTML body sent by res.redirect() when HTML is accepted now has , and <body> wrappers instead of a bare <p> fragment
app.render(view, null, callback) is now treated like omitted or empty options instead of throwing on the null locals
res.send() keeps the existing parameters of a Content-Type when it appends charset (text/plain; foo=bar -> text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8) instead of dropping them
res.send() no longer throws when the response's Content-Type header fails to parse; it leaves the header as set
The default error handler logs the whole error object (including cause and library-specific properties) instead of only err.stack
res.attachment(), res.download() and res.sendFile() now emit Content-Disposition filenames that are valid HTTP tokens without quotes (filename=user.html) where they were always quoted before
express.json/urlencoded/raw/text (body-parser 2.3) throw at parser construction when the limit option is invalid instead of silently disabling the body size limit
VertexAIBackend is deprecated in favor of the new AgentPlatformBackend, whose default location is global instead of us-central1.
initializeAppCheck() must again be given a provider; the provider-less call added in 12.15.0 is removed.
In Node, Firestore's HTTP/2 flow-control window defaults to 256 KB instead of 64 KB (new grpcFlowControlWindow setting to change it).
All Imagen APIs are removed from firebase/ai (getImagenModel, getTemplateImagenModel, ImagenModel, TemplateImagenModel and the Imagen* config/response/enum types); use Gemini image models instead.
FunctionsError from callable functions includes the HTTP status code in its message and the request URL in customData, changing the message text for the same failure.

Storage and persistence errors during Auth current-user updates are wrapped in a FirebaseError with code auth/internal-error (original under customData.originalError) instead of propagating the raw exception.

TemplateGenerativeModel.generateContent()/generateContentStream() take a single TemplateRequest object ({ templateId, templateVariables, toolConfig? }) instead of separate templateId and variables arguments, and templateVariables is required in TemplateRequest and StartTemplateChatParams.
VertexAIBackend and BackendType.VERTEX_AI are removed; use AgentPlatformBackend (default location global; pass 'us-central1' to keep the old one).

Other long-deprecated AI Logic APIs are removed: AI.location, LiveSession.sendMediaChunks()/sendMediaStream(), LanguageModelCreateCoreOptions.topK/temperature, GoogleMaps.enableWidget, GroundingMetadata.retrievalQueries and CountTokensResponse.totalBillableCharacters.
The default in-cloud model for hybrid inference changes from gemini-2.5-flash-lite to gemini-3.5-flash-lite.
AI Part types become a discriminated union with an explicit type property (plus UnknownPart), type discriminators are stripped before sending, and chat history is deep-copied.
firebase/ai exports ChatSession as an interface instead of a class, so it can no longer be constructed or used as a value.
candidateCount, temperature, topP, topK, presencePenalty and frequencyPenalty are deprecated in GenerationConfig and LiveGenerationConfig.
The minimum supported Node.js version is 24.12.0 (engines in all @firebase packages), up from 20.
Firestore's UpdateData<T> type changes to accept indexed types and Record<X, T> for T (commit marked breaking).

framer-motion no longer picks up the optional @emotion/is-prop-valid peer on its own to decide which props reach the DOM (it is dropped from peerDependencies); apps that relied on it must pass it explicitly with <MotionConfig isValidProp={isPropValid}> or wrap the styled component with motion.create
scroll() progress callbacks are no longer driven by a native ScrollTimeline where the browser supports one; they always use main-thread scroll measurement (scrollInfo)
scroll()/useScroll animations that use an offset now run on the main thread for every offset, instead of being hardware-accelerated through ScrollTimeline/ViewTimeline

The internal observeTimeline export (re-exported from motion-dom) is removed; it was dropped in 13.5.0, restored in 13.5.1 for compatibility, and is gone from 14.0.0, which also pins exact framer-motion/motion-dom/motion-utils versions instead of ^ ranges

On the MotionPath interface (the object a path factory like arc() returns for transition.path), animateVisualElement becomes optional and @deprecated in favour of the new animateValues hook, which also runs for elements animated with animate()
contentSecurityPolicy() now throws for directive names that don't start with a lowercase letter or that end in a hyphen (e.g. 'DefaultSrc', 'Default-Src', '-default-src'), which it accepted before
contentSecurityPolicy({ useDefaults: false }) without directives is now a type error and throws at runtime ('has no directives'); before, omitted directives defaulted to the default directive set
process.getBuiltinModule() inside a test now returns the sandbox's process and the hooked node:module rather than the host runtime's

Calling module.register() or module.registerHooks() inside a test now throws an actionable error; before, the hooks silently attached to the loader running Jest itself and stayed registered for later test files in the worker

On Node 24.9+, resolution and import-attribute errors anywhere in an ESM graph are raised before any of its CommonJS dependencies execute (Node's run-nothing-on-a-broken-graph order); older Node keeps the previous linking-time execution order

The default resolver now honors the module-sync export condition, so a package exposing an ESM entry point for require() resolves to the file Node would pick instead of failing with Cannot find module
When Node runs with --preserve-symlinks or NODE_PRESERVE_SYMLINKS=1 the default resolver no longer realpaths symlinked modules, matching Node; before it always resolved symlinks to their targets
@jest/source-map's exported getCallsite() is deprecated in favor of SourceMapSupport#getCallsite
@jest/environment-jsdom-abstract (and so jest-environment-jsdom) now declares @types/jsdom as a peer dependency the project must satisfy instead of bundling it as a dependency

A file with ESM syntax inside a package that declares "type":"commonjs", or with a .cjs extension, now throws the CommonJS SyntaxError as Node does; since 30.4.0 Jest had retried it and silently loaded it as native ESM (and without vm modules reported ERR_REQUIRE_ESM)

reporters, coverageReporters, workerIdleMemoryLimit, cwd and runnerOptions are removed from the project config types and, like maxWorkers and coverageThreshold, now trigger a validation warning when set in a project config instead of being silently ignored
The optional canvas peer dependency range is raised from ^3.0.0 to ^3.2.3

window.close() no longer tears down the window's document: retained references to the document and its DOM stay usable after closing (scripts, timers, resource loads and queued events in the closed document are still stopped)
The history icon is renamed rotate-ccw-clock (same artwork): RotateCcwClock is the canonical export and History remains only as an alias of it, flagged deprecated in the icon metadata
The podcast icon is replaced by the new mic-signal and mic-audio-lines icons: Podcast remains only as an alias of MicSignal and now renders the mic-signal artwork instead of the old podcast design

The emoticon icons are redrawn and renamed after their Unicode emoji: angry→face-angry, annoyed→face-expressionless, laugh→face-grinning, meh→face-neutral, frown→face-slightly-frowning, smile→face-slightly-smiling, smile-plus→face-slightly-smiling-plus; Angry, Annoyed, Laugh, Meh, Frown, Smile and SmilePlus remain as aliases of the new exports

The trash icon's own design is removed in favour of trash-2: the Trash export now renders the former trash-2 artwork and Trash2 remains only as an alias of Trash (its metadata marks the alias deprecated), where before they were two different icons

The absoluteStrokeWidth prop (on icon components and LucideProvider) is marked @deprecated in favour of the new nonScalingStroke prop, which sets vector-effect=non-scaling-stroke on the paths instead of rescaling stroke-width

Per-icon ESM modules (lucide-react/dist/esm/icons/<name>.mjs; the CJS build is a single bundle) export __iconData, an object {name, size, node}, instead of the bare __iconNode node array; __iconNode is only declared (as deprecated) in the types and is no longer exported at runtime, and DynamicIconModule now reads __iconData
The exported IconNode type is marked @deprecated in favour of LucideIconNode[] (and the new LucideIconData object type); IconNode's element names widen from an SVG tag-name union to string
SwissFranc, BadgeSwissFranc and ReceiptSwissFranc are marked @deprecated (the depicted symbol is obsolete), where before they carried no deprecation tag

flip-horizontal-2 and flip-vertical-2 are renamed triangles-centerline-dashed-horizontal and triangles-centerline-dashed-vertical; FlipHorizontal2 and FlipVertical2 remain as aliases of the new TrianglesCenterlineDashedHorizontal/Vertical exports

Three icons are renamed: album→square-bookmark and book-marked→book-bookmark (both also redrawn), building-2→building-complex; Album, BookMarked and Building2 remain only as aliases of the new SquareBookmark, BookBookmark and BuildingComplex exports

The numbered music icons are renamed after the notes they show: music→eighth-notes, music-2→eighth-note, music-3→half-note, music-4→sixteenth-notes (three of them redrawn); Music, Music2, Music3 and Music4 remain only as aliases of the new exports

The Ukrainian ('uk') locale's week-of-year config changes from doy 7 to doy 4, so week(), weeks() and the 'w'/'ww' format tokens follow ISO 8601 (week 1 is the week containing Jan 4) instead of the week containing Jan 7; week numbers around the new year differ

Month names output by format() change in three locales: Indonesian ('id') short August is 'Agu' instead of 'Agt' (both still parse), Polish ('pl') 'D. MMMM' uses the genitive ('14. lutego' instead of '14. luty'), and Catalan ('ca') format-context month names use a typographic apostrophe (d’abril, d’agost, d’octubre instead of d'abril…)
Weekday names change in two locales: Swedish ('sv') short Thursday is 'tors' instead of 'tor', and Ukrainian ('uk') Friday forms use U+02BC (пʼятниця) instead of U+2019
The 'L' long-date format changes for Georgian ('ka'), from DD/MM/YYYY to DD.MM.YYYY, and for Dutch (Belgium) ('nl-be'), from DD/MM/YYYY to D/MM/YYYY

calendar() output changes in two locales: Portuguese (Brazil) ('pt-br') uses 'à' instead of 'às' before times under 2 o'clock ('Hoje à 1:00'), and Swahili ('sw') writes 'saa' instead of 'saat' and puts the weekday first in next/last-week phrases ('Jumatatu ijayo saa …' instead of 'wiki ijayo Jumatatu saat …')

fromNow()/from()/humanize() output changes in three locales: Hungarian ('hu') keeps the number in suffixed relative seconds, Uzbek ('uz', 'uz-latn') past values drop the 'Bir necha'/'Бир неча' prefix ('5 kun oldin' instead of 'Bir necha 5 kun oldin'), and Swahili ('sw') past values use per-unit 'iliyopita'/'zilizopita'/'uliopita' suffixes instead of the 'tokea …' prefix

German locales ('de', 'de-at', 'de-ch') now parse short month names without the trailing dot ('Feb', 'Mär', 'Jun', 'Jul'), where before such input matched no month and the parsed date silently fell back to January
A file whose size is exactly limits.fileSize is now accepted; before, reaching the limit exactly raised LIMIT_FILE_SIZE
file.originalname now decodes the WHATWG multipart escapes %0A, %0D and %22 to LF, CR and a double quote instead of keeping the escaped text
The middleware calls next() inside the caller's async context, so AsyncLocalStorage stores set before multer are visible in later handlers (they were lost before)
Field names now decode %0A, %0D and %22 like file.originalname: req.body keys, file.fieldname and err.field carry the real name instead of the escaped spelling

multer() throws a TypeError at construction when a limits value is not a non-negative integer or Infinity (e.g. a float or a string), where before such a value was accepted and silently disabled that limit
A request with exactly limits.parts parts is now accepted; LIMIT_PART_COUNT fires only when the count exceeds the limit (it fired on reaching it before)
Files rejected by fileFilter no longer use up a field's maxCount in upload.array()/upload.fields(), so later files in that field are still accepted
The LIMIT_UNEXPECTED_FILE MulterError message changed from 'Unexpected field' to 'Unexpected file field'
getToken() returns null when the Authorization header's Bearer value is malformed percent-encoding instead of throwing from decodeURIComponent

OAuth state, nonce and PKCE check cookies now record the provider that minted them and the callback throws when a different provider handles it; before any provider's callback accepted them (sign-ins in flight across the upgrade fail once)

The email provider's default identifier normalizer applies Unicode NFKC normalization before validating the address, so homoglyphs of '@' are collapsed and rejected; before validation ran on the raw string
An explicitly configured NEXTAUTH_URL now takes precedence over the auto-detected forwarded host when VERCEL or AUTH_TRUST_HOST is set; before the forwarded host won in trusted-host mode
On the 15.5 line, Next.js now refuses to run with TypeScript >= 7.0 and exits with an error (the 16.x line gained TypeScript 7 support instead).
`experimental.cachedNavigations` is on by default for apps with `cacheComponents: true`, so 'use cache' content is reused from the client cache across navigations unless set to `false`.

`unstable_catchError` from `next/error` is renamed to `catchError`, and the `unstable_retry` prop passed to `error.js`/`global-error.js` boundaries and `catchError` fallbacks is renamed to `retry`; no `unstable_` aliases remain.

Undocumented methods on the custom-server `next()` instance (`setAssetPrefix()`, `revalidate()`, logging helpers and the legacy `render*` helpers) are deprecated with warnings; use `getRequestHandler()`.
The Edge runtime (`export const runtime = 'edge'`) and the `preferredRegion` route segment config are deprecated with build warnings and `@deprecated` types; the Node.js runtime is the path forward.

Removed experimental config keys: `experimental.turbopackMemoryLimit` and `experimental.viewTransition` (view transitions work without a flag), and, merged here under the same-kind rule, keys whose feature is now always on or folded elsewhere: `experimental.rootParams` (`next/root-params` works without a flag), `experimental.turbopackImportTypeText` (`import ... with { type: 'text' }` on by default), `experimental.partialFallbacks` (now part of `partialPrefetching`), `experimental.instantNavigationDevToolsToggle` (Navigation Inspector shown whenever `cacheComponents` is on), `experimental.immutableAssetToken` (replaced by `supportsImmutableAssets` and an `_next/static/immutable/` path prefix) and `experimental.imgOptSkipMetadata`.

The instant segment config object changes shape: the required `prefetch: 'static' | 'runtime'` option is removed (prefetching is now set by the separate `export const prefetch` segment config), and `samples`/`from` become `unstable_samples`/`unstable_from`; `instant` also accepts `true`.

The reworked App Router scroll and focus handling (`experimental.appNewScrollHandler`) is on by default: after navigation the active element is blurred instead of focusing the first focusable element in the segment.

When `next dev` detects a coding agent (env vars such as `CLAUDECODE`), it now creates or updates a managed block in the project's `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` pointing at the bundled docs; opt out with `agentRules: false`.
The `opengraph-image` (and sibling image route) default export's return type is narrowed to `Response`; the other return types the types previously allowed failed the build.
`experimental.optimisticRouting` (client-side route prediction) is on by default, changing when navigations commit and which segments are fetched.
Requests to unknown paths whose `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is not a document (images, workers, manifest icons) now get a plain-text 404 instead of rendering the HTML not-found page.
`experimental.prefetchInlining` is on by default: small segment prefetches are bundled into one response per link instead of one request per segment.
`enablePrerenderSourceMaps` now defaults to `true` for every app (previously only when `cacheComponents` was on), so errors thrown while prerendering in `next build` are source-mapped.
Turbopack filesystem caching for `next build` (`experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`) is now on by default, so repeat builds reuse artifacts from `.next/cache`.
`experimental.turbopackTreeShaking` is renamed to `experimental.turbopackModuleFragments`.
`next build` type-checks with the project's TypeScript CLI by default (`experimental.useTypeScriptCli`, opt out with `false`) instead of the compiler API.
The `export const unstable_instant` route segment config is renamed to `instant` (stabilized); `unstable_instant` is no longer read.

`experimental.validateRSCRequestHeaders` is on by default: an RSC request whose headers do not match the client's cache-busting search parameter is no longer served as an RSC response (previously only validated when opted in).
`experimental.varyParams` is on by default: cached navigation/prefetch entries are keyed only on the params a segment actually reads instead of on all params.
The `experimental.appNewScrollHandler` config key is removed; the new scroll/focus handling (default since 16.3.0) can no longer be turned off.
Turbopack production builds now generate shorter CSS Module class names (development keeps the long readable names).
Pages Router support for React 18 is deprecated: `next dev`/`next build` warn when React 18 is installed, ahead of removal in 17.

Client-side-rendering bailouts (`useSearchParams` without Suspense, resumed-render and CSR bailouts) now use React's `ReactDOM.browser` mechanism by default instead of throwing the Next.js bailout errors.

`experimental.strictRouteMatching` is on by default: App Router URLs that cannot build a complete route tree are rejected, unreachable pages and incompatible parallel-route slots are reported, and interception routes need a canonical route; `deprecated.looseRouteMatching: true` is the escape hatch.
Turbopack production builds now mangle internal export names by default (`experimental.turbopackMangleExportNames`), shortening the names used to connect modules.
Turbopack now emits its runtime as one chunk shared across routes (`experimental.turbopackSharedRuntime` on by default) instead of a per-route runtime.
Unrecognized Server Action IDs now return 400 (malformed) or 409 (unknown in this deployment) for both fetch and MPA form submissions, instead of 404 or 500.
`useReportWebVitals` moves to web-vitals v6: the FID metric is no longer reported and CLS/INP/LCP are now also reported for soft navigations with a `navigationURL`.

sendMail() now fails a message whose deduped envelope (To, Cc and Bcc together) has more than 100000 recipients: the new maxRecipients option defaults to 100000 (0 or Infinity lifts it), where before there was no cap
The minimum Node.js version rises from 6 to 20 (engines.node >=20.0.0) with the move to a TypeScript-built dual ESM/CommonJS package

nodemailer ships its own TypeScript declarations, which take precedence over @types/nodemailer; 10.0.1 and 10.0.11 restored most of the @types layout (namespaces such as Mail.Options, SMTPTransport.Options), but internal underscore members are not declared and some types are stricter than the community typings

SMTP server replies are capped by the new maxResponseSize option, 1 MB by default: a server reply (or unterminated line) larger than that drops the connection with an EPROTOCOL error, where before the client buffered without limit

Pooled transports stop requeueing a message whose connection closed while sending after maxRequeues attempts, which now defaults to 5 (before: unlimited when unset), and retry with exponential backoff (50 ms doubling to 2 s) instead of immediately
Content fetched from a URL (attachment or alternative href) now has a default 60 s inactivity timeout and a 64 MB response size limit, where before neither was bounded
When requireTLS is set together with ignoreTLS or opportunisticTLS, requireTLS now wins (the connection must upgrade to TLS) instead of the combination silently resolving to plaintext
Pooled SMTP connections that sit idle are closed after 4 minutes by default (new idleTimeout option), where before an idle pooled connection stayed open until the server dropped it

connectionTimeout now bounds the whole session setup (DNS lookup, proxy handshake, TCP, TLS, greeting and STARTTLS) instead of only the TCP connect, and the STARTTLS handshake also times out after greetingTimeout; a server that pauses before its greeting longer than connectionTimeout now fails with ETIMEDOUT (timeoutType GREETING_TIMEOUT)
With opportunisticTLS, when the server refuses STARTTLS the client continues in plaintext but no longer authenticates on the unencrypted connection (AUTH stays disabled)
When the server advertises PIPELINING, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO and DATA are sent in one batch (RFC 2920) instead of one command per round trip
SMTP sockets enable TCP keepalive after 30 s of idle time and run with Nagle off (noDelay), and a socket the server never closes is destroyed after close()
SMTPConnection emits only 'end', not an ECONNECTION 'error', when the server closes an idle connection or sends an idle 421

Any 421 reply now ends the SMTP session: the command gets its own error (EAUTH, EENVELOPE, …), queued replies are not waited for and the message in flight fails once, where before a server that answered 421 but kept the socket open left the send waiting until the socket timeout

A host with several addresses is connected to with happy eyeballs / net.connect autoSelectFamily, each address getting a share of connectionTimeout, and a failed TLS handshake no longer moves on to the next address
In a pooled transport a message the server rejects is followed by RSET and the connection is kept for the next message
In a pooled transport a message whose reused connection was dropped by the server before any of it was sent is requeued instead of failed

A content stream (attachment, html, raw) that is destroyed without an error, or was already read, now fails the send, where before the send waited forever or went out with an empty attachment; a failed send now releases the files and HTTP requests it was reading
The sendmail transport reports the process exit code instead of EPIPE, and a sendmail process that exits (even with 0) before the message was written, or is killed by a signal, is now an error

A per-message auth object passed to sendMail() may set only credential fields (type, user, pass, accessToken, refreshToken, expires); accessUrl, clientId, clientSecret and the other OAuth2/transport settings are taken from the transport only and are ignored at message level
Fetching URL content gets an overall maxTime deadline for the whole request including redirects, two minutes by default, on top of the 10.0.12 inactivity timeout
The DKIM body cache file (cacheDir) is created with mode 0600 instead of the process default

addressparser no longer caps nested address groups: members past 50 levels of nesting (10 in 10.1.4 and 10.1.5) used to be dropped, now groups are read in one pass and no members are dropped at any depth

The prompt_cache_retention request parameter (Chat Completions and Responses create/compact) and the Response.prompt_cache_retention field are marked @deprecated in favour of the new prompt_cache_options.ttl
Minimum supported Node.js rises from 20 to 22 (package.json engines >=22.0.0 added, Node version policy codified); Node 20 is no longer supported
embeddings.create called with encoding_format 'base64' now resolves to a response whose data[].embedding is typed string instead of number[] (a new overload); runtime behavior is unchanged
The Sora video API surface (client.videos and its create/retrieve/list/delete/remix/edit/extend/downloadContent/character methods) is marked @deprecated

The error field of MCP tool call items (ResponseOutputItem.McpCall, ResponseItem.McpCall, ResponseInputItem.McpCall, ConversationItem.McpCall) changes from string | null to a structured McpToolCallError object union (mcp_protocol_error / mcp_tool_execution_error / http_error)

ParsedChatCompletionMessage.tool_calls (from chat.completions.parse and ChatCompletionStream snapshots) is typed as an array of ParsedFunctionToolCall | ChatCompletionMessageCustomToolCall instead of ParsedFunctionToolCall only, so reading .function without narrowing on type no longer type-checks
The geography parameter of admin project create/update (ProjectCreateParams/ProjectUpdateParams) is marked @deprecated in favour of the new residency parameter
The name field is removed from ResponseFunctionCallArgumentsDoneEvent (the response.function_call_arguments.done stream event); code reading event.name no longer type-checks
connector_id on the MCP tool (Responses Tool.Mcp and the Realtime MCP tool configs) is marked @deprecated; use server_url for a remote MCP server or tunnel_id for a Secure MCP Tunnel
Legacy DALL-E image surface marked @deprecated: images.createVariation(), the response_format parameter of images.generate/edit, and the style parameter of images.generate
The user parameter of images.generate and images.edit is marked @deprecated in favour of the new safety_identifier parameter (still used when safety_identifier is omitted)

Passing an invalid Date (e.g. new Date(undefined)) as a query parameter now emits a DeprecationWarning (code PG_INVALID_DATE) while still serializing the garbage NaN string; it is slated to become an error in the next major, where 8.22 serialized it silently.
preact/compat flushSync now batches the state updates made inside its callback into one synchronous render instead of rendering once per setter
Supported browsers raised to Chrome 71 / Safari 12.1 / Firefox 69 / Edge 79 without polyfills; IE11 support dropped
Minimum supported TypeScript version raised to 5.1

Core and add-on bundles ship only as .mjs ES modules; the .module.js, CommonJS, UMD and .min builds are removed (require('preact') works only via require(esm)), and exports.browser became exports.module
The exports maps in the nested package.json files of subpackages (hooks, compat, debug, jsx-runtime, ...) are removed; resolution goes through the root package.json exports
ref passed to a component is now forwarded as an ordinary prop (ref on a function component reaches its props) instead of pointing at the component instance; forwardRef is no longer needed
Hook dependency arrays and useState/useReducer bail-outs compare with Object.is instead of ===, so NaN is treated as unchanged (and +0/-0 as different)
Core no longer appends px to numeric style values (style={{height: 500}} renders height:500); the automatic px suffix only applies with preact/compat
defaultProps on components is only applied when preact/compat is loaded; core Preact ignores it
The optional third replaceNode parameter of render() is removed (use preact-root-fragment's createRootFragment instead)
Component.base (the component's root DOM node) is removed from class component instances
SuspenseList is removed from preact/compat
useEffect cleanups of an unmounting component now run after paint (deferred like React) instead of synchronously during unmount
useRef's type now requires an initial value, and RefObject<T> describes current as exactly T (include null in T where needed)

The JSX namespace keeps only the types TypeScript needs (Element, IntrinsicElements, ...); DOM attribute types such as JSX.ButtonHTMLAttributes move to the preact namespace (import { ButtonHTMLAttributes } from 'preact')
The deprecated ForwardFn type is removed from preact/compat
JSX types restrict the role attribute of , , , and

Event handler props whose name has an uppercase letter after 'on' (onMyEvent) always listen for the lowercased event (myevent); Preact 10 kept the original casing for events the DOM element didn't know
Re-rendering the same (hoisted, constant) vnode object no longer skips diffing that subtree; it is diffed like any other vnode
The check for whether a DOM sibling is still mounted uses parentNode presence instead of contains(); listed under breaking changes, effect on application code unclear
The optional peer dependency preact-render-to-string is raised from >=5 to >=6.7.0
Hydration 2.0: suspended boundaries are hydrated against comment markers emitted by the server renderer, allowing 0 or 2+ DOM nodes per async boundary instead of exactly one
When reordering children Preact uses Element.moveBefore() where the browser supports it instead of insertBefore(), preserving state such as focus and iframe content of moved nodes
When an already-revealed Suspense boundary suspends again, its components keep their committed hook state (effects are cleaned up and re-run on reveal) instead of resetting it
preact/compat reports React version 19.0.0 (its exported version) instead of the 18.x it reported before
The list of unitless CSS properties that don't get an automatic px suffix (now a preact/compat feature) was made more accurate, changing which numeric style values get px
The prisma mcp server no longer exposes a migrate-reset tool; an agent must run prisma migrate reset through the CLI (where the AI safety checkpoint applies) instead.

prisma db push --accept-data-loss now goes through the AI safety checkpoint and refuses to run under a detected AI agent without explicit user consent (PRISMA_USER_CONSENT_FOR_DANGEROUS_AI_ACTION); before, only --force-reset, db drop and migrate reset were guarded.

The AI safety checkpoint detects many more agents (Codex CLI on Linux, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Cline, Goose, Amp, Crush, Augment, Antigravity, Replit Agent, Devin, and generic AI_AGENT/AGENT variables), so destructive commands now refuse in environments that used to pass.
prisma init now installs the prisma/skills agent-skill catalog into the new project by default (opt out with --no-skills), where it used to scaffold only the schema, config and .env.
On Windows, engine binaries are cached in a user-level %APPDATA%\Prisma directory instead of the cwd-relative node_modules\.cache.
Prisma Studio's SQL execution, linting and navigation resolve unqualified identifiers against the schema selected in Studio instead of always the adapter's default schema.

Without --config, the Prisma 7 CLI looks first for root prisma7.config.* files, then .config/prisma7.*, and only then falls back to prisma.config.*; a prisma7.config.* that fails to load is reported instead of falling back.
prisma init in new projects writes prisma7.config.ts instead of prisma.config.ts.
Prisma Studio's local server binds to 127.0.0.1 instead of all interfaces, rejects browser requests from origins other than its own localhost URL, and stops sending wildcard CORS headers.
prisma generate may now show a one-time interactive prompt offering to install Prisma's agent skills (skipped in CI, containers, hooks, lifecycle scripts, watch mode and with --no-hints).
A globally installed prisma CLI now warns during prisma generate when its version differs from the project's local prisma or @prisma/client.
The AI safety checkpoint also covers interactive prisma db push data-loss confirmations, not only runs with --accept-data-loss.

A statement that Prisma Client splits into several chunks (too many bind values, e.g. a large deleteMany or read) now runs inside a transaction and is rolled back if a later chunk fails, where earlier chunks used to stay committed.
An invalid Date passed to $queryRaw/$executeRaw throws PrismaClientValidationError instead of a generic error.

Bytes values returned by queries and raw queries are Uint8Arrays that own a standalone ArrayBuffer, instead of views into Node's shared Buffer pool (whose .buffer exposed unrelated bytes and an 8192 byteLength).

The recursive path types (Path, FieldPath and the name types built on them) stop at 10 segments: a field name nested 11 or more levels deep is no longer a valid path for register, setValue, watch etc., where before every depth was generated

When a change event from an <input type="file"> is passed to a controlled field's onChange (Controller / useController field.onChange), the stored value is the input's FileList instead of its string value (the fake C:\fakepath\… path)

The <FormStateSubscribe> render-prop component is renamed <FormState> (props type FormStateSubscribeProps → FormStateProps); FormStateSubscribe and FormStateSubscribeProps remain only as @deprecated aliases
handleSubmit(onValid)(event) now resolves to the value returned by onValid (Promise<Awaited<TResult> | undefined>, generic over TResult) instead of always resolving to undefined (typed Promise<void>)
`href()` now stringifies and URL-encodes param values (splats encoded per segment), matching `generatePath()`, instead of interpolating them raw.
`href()` and `generatePath()` encode path params with RFC 3986 path-segment rules instead of `encodeURIComponent`, so `$ & + , ; = : @` stay literal (`1.0.0+1` no longer becomes `1.0.0%2B1`).
The `createStaticRouter({ branches })` option is deprecated: it is ignored with a warning (branches are cached internally), and `EntryContext.branches` is now always an empty array.

The exported `UNSAFE_DataRouterStateContext` no longer holds the full `RouterState`; loader/action data and pending navigation state move to the new `UNSAFE_DataRouterDataContext` and `UNSAFE_DataRouterNavigationContext`.

React Router's view transition APIs are deprecated in favor of React 19.3's `<ViewTransition>`: the `viewTransition` prop/option on `Link`, `NavLink`, `Form`, `navigate`/`submit`, `useViewTransitionState`, and `NavLink`'s `isTransitioning` render prop and `transitioning` class.
React DOM passes Trusted Types objects (TrustedHTML/TrustedScript/TrustedScriptURL) through to DOM sinks instead of coercing them to strings, so they now work under a require-trusted-types-for CSP
Concurrent transitions render independently instead of being entangled into one render, so a slow transition no longer delays unrelated ones
DEV now warns when a component appears to have been unblocked by calling use() conditionally, which was silent before
In StrictMode effects are now double-invoked during hydration too, matching client-rendered roots, where hydrated roots were previously exempt
StrictMode's DEV double-invocation no longer re-runs effects for children that only moved (were reordered) rather than remounted
Rendering data-block <script> elements (non-executable types such as application/json) no longer triggers a DEV warning
React.lazy now treats the resolved module's .default export as the canonical component type for identity comparisons instead of the lazy wrapper's own resolution
The DEV DOM-nesting validation for <select> follows the new HTML <select> parser rules, changing which children are allowed inside <select> without a warning
The list of CSS shorthand properties behind the DEV shorthand/longhand style-conflict warning was updated, changing which style combinations warn
defaultValue on <input type=number> is now synced to the DOM the same way as on other input types instead of the number-specific handling used before
credentialless on <iframe> is now a recognized boolean attribute (true renders the bare attribute, false omits it) instead of being rendered as a stringified unknown attribute
When React automatically resets a form after its action completes, the form's onReset handler now fires; previously the automatic reset did not fire it
The FormData handed to a form action is now built with the submitter, so the submitting button's name/value is included as in the native FormData constructor; before it was left out
State updates triggered by resize events are batched until the next frame instead of being processed per event
react-dom/server streaming APIs no longer call onAllReady after the shell has errored, where previously it could still fire
During server-rendering error recovery a tree that never completed is now treated as an error instead of being accepted as finished
The API version the SDK pins and sends by default changes from 2026-06-24.dahlia to 2026-07-29.dahlia

Fields typed as non-exhaustive ("open") enums now include a shared OtherString type (string & Record<never, never>) in their unions, so they are no longer closed literal unions (exhaustive switches and assignments to literal-union types stop type-checking)
Limited-use request parameters removed: proof_of_registration on AccountCreateParams.documents and dynamic_tax_rates on Checkout.SessionCreateParams.line_items[]
The API version the SDK pins and sends by default changes from 2026-07-29.dahlia to 2026-08-26.dahlia
Serializing a V2 request parameter that is a discriminated union now throws when its discriminator is missing or not a string, instead of sending it without int64/decimal coercion
cryptogram is removed from payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure on PaymentAttemptRecord and PaymentRecord
Webhook verification helpers (webhooks.constructEvent and the signature verifiers) throw when given an empty webhook secret instead of computing a signature with it
The pinned default API version moves to the new major API release 2026-09-30.endive (from 2026-08-26.dahlia), bringing that release's breaking API changes
Node.js 18 support is dropped; Node.js 20 is the minimum supported version
Stripe.V2List<T> no longer declares the V1-only object, has_more and url fields (never populated); V2 lists paginate with next_page_url / previous_page_url
V2 request address properties are typed with operation-specific V2 interfaces instead of the shared V1 Stripe.AddressParam / Stripe.JapanAddressParam types
The Stripe.ErrorType type namespace is removed; use Stripe.errors (e.g. Stripe.errors.StripeCardError) in type annotations
A response whose body stalls or is cut off before completion now throws StripeConnectionError instead of StripeAPIError
webhooks.signature.verifyHeader() and verifyHeaderAsync() check the timestamp against Webhook.DEFAULT_TOLERANCE when tolerance is omitted, instead of skipping the timestamp check; pass 0 to skip
webhooks.constructEvent() with tolerance 0 now skips timestamp verification instead of applying the default tolerance
AccountRejectParams.reason (accounts.reject) is typed as an enum of allowed values instead of string

New values (marked breaking) on existing response enums: requirements errors[].code (invalid_address_cmra_address, invalid_address_registered_agent_address), Reserve.Plan.status/type (other, manual_release), Reserve.Release.reason (hold_expired), V2 account capability status (rejected) and status_details[].code (rejected_*)
The value bulk_hold_expiry is removed from the Reserve.Release.reason enum
Charge.payment_method_details.card.mandate changes from string to expandable(Mandate) (string | Stripe.Mandate)

The payment_method_types request parameter is removed from Checkout.SessionCreateParams, PaymentIntentCreateParams/UpdateParams/ConfirmParams and SetupIntentCreateParams/UpdateParams (use allowed_payment_method_types)

Checkout.Session.payment_method_options.bancontact.setup_future_usage and PaymentIntent.payment_method_options.blik.setup_future_usage change from the literal 'none' to the enum 'none' | 'off_session'
countries is removed from FinancialConnections.Session.filters and FinancialConnections.SessionCreateParams.filters (use country)

The billing_cycle_anchor parameter of SubscriptionUpdateParams, SubscriptionResumeParams and InvoiceCreatePreviewParams.subscription_details changes from 'now' | 'unchanged' (| timestamp) to the new billing_cycle_anchor_param type
payto is removed from PaymentMethodUpdateParams
Radar.PaymentEvaluation.signals.fraudulent_payment.score changes from number to number | null
configurations is removed from use_case.account_onboarding and use_case.account_update on V2.Core.AccountLink and V2.Core.AccountLinkCreateParams
target es5, deprecated in 6.0, is removed: it is a hard error that ignoreDeprecations no longer silences, and es2015 is the lowest target.
downlevelIteration, deprecated in 6.0, is removed; setting it is a hard error.
moduleResolution node (node10), deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; nodenext or bundler replaces it.
The module values amd, umd, system and none, deprecated in 6.0, are removed and are hard errors; esnext or preserve with a bundler replaces them.
The /// <amd-module /> directive, deprecated in 6.0, is removed together with module amd.
baseUrl, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; paths entries must be written relative to the project root.
moduleResolution classic, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
esModuleInterop can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape); interop import semantics are always on.
allowSyntheticDefaultImports can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape).
alwaysStrict is always true and setting it to false is a hard error; sloppy-mode code is no longer accepted.
outFile, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
module Foo {} namespace syntax, deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only namespace Foo {} is accepted.
The asserts keyword on imports (and assert in import() options), deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only with is accepted.
/// <reference no-default-lib /> directives, deprecated in 6.0, are no longer respected at all, including under skipDefaultLibCheck.

The typescript package no longer exports the compiler API: lib/typescript.js and typescript.d.ts are gone and import ts from "typescript" only yields the version; tools must alias typescript to @typescript/typescript6 until a new API ships in 7.1.

Inference through template literal types consumes whole Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so `${infer H}${infer T}` on a string starting with an emoji yields the emoji and the rest rather than two surrogate halves; type-level string utilities that counted code units break.
The package's engines field requires Node.js >=16.20.0, up from >=14.17 in 5.9 and 6.0.
The tsserver executable and lib/tsserver.js are no longer shipped (bin holds only tsc); editors integrate through the new Language Server Protocol server instead.

In JavaScript files, Closure-era JSDoc forms are no longer recognized: a standalone ? type, module:path namepath types, @class/@constructor, @enum, identifier-named typedefs (/** @typedef {T} */ Name;), function(string): void function types, postfix ! and bare values used as types (write typeof v).

In JavaScript files, constructor functions (this.x inside a function plus prototype assignments), fallback initializers (f.x = f.x || v), nested undeclared expandos (N.X.Y = {}), typed this.x; declarations without an initializer, this aliases (var that = this) and top-level this as globalThis are no longer treated as declarations, and expando assignments of void 0 are no longer ignored; use classes and explicit assignments.

In CommonJS JavaScript files, nested undeclared exports (exports.N.X.p = 1), an ignored empty module.exports = {}, this as an alias of module.exports, var x = require("m").prop, aliasing module.exports to a variable and mixing module.exports = ... with module.exports.x = ... are no longer supported, and repeated exports.x assignments union instead of narrowing.

Types and symbols are ordered by a deterministic content-based algorithm (6.0's stableTypeOrdering flag) and this cannot be turned off, so union member order in declaration emit and hovers, and occasionally inference results, differ from 6.0's default ordering by type ID.
Conflicting declarations are reported at every contributing declaration instead of sometimes only one, so conflicts that skipLibCheck previously hid entirely now surface in non-.d.ts files.
Declaration (.d.ts) emit from .js input files is rewritten and no longer matches 6.0's output, especially when the input has errors; supported JSDoc tags keep their semantics.

JSDoc in .js files follows TypeScript rules: a variadic {...T} is only an array synonym and no longer makes a parameter a rest parameter, {T=} no longer adds undefined when strictNullChecks is off, an asserts return annotation on an arrow must go on the variable's @type, @typedef and @callback in a class body hoist out of it, a @param applies to at most one function, @type assertions block narrowing, and @overload is ignored on arrow and function expressions.

Calls in .js files use TypeScript's arity rules: with strict false, arguments for parameters typed undefined, unknown or any can no longer be omitted, and using arguments inside a function body no longer implies a ...args: any[] parameter.

The exported _getStandardProps(schema) utility is removed and replaced by _standardSchema(schema), which eagerly attaches the ~standard properties and returns the schema; custom schemas that built their ~standard getter with _getStandardProps no longer compile.

Direct .wasm imports (the WASM ESM Integration added in 8.1.0) now expose exported WebAssembly.Global values as their plain JS values instead of WebAssembly.Global objects, so import { g } from "./m.wasm" gives the number rather than an object read through g.value.

Direct .wasm imports are now compiled and instantiated with the JS String Builtins and Imported String Constants proposals enabled (matching the spec and Node.js), so modules importing wasm:js-string or string constants link differently than before.

With the default bundle config loader, Vite now warns when vite.config uses features the native loader (configLoader: "native", planned to become the default in a future major) does not support: __dirname/__filename in ESM, extensionless imports, directory index imports, JSON imports without a with { type: "json" } attribute, and ESM syntax in a file Node loads as CommonJS; VITE_CONFIG_NATIVE_IGNORE_WARNING=true silences it.

The native-loader compatibility warning now also flags named imports from JSON modules in vite.config (import { version } from "./package.json"), since JSON modules only have a default export per spec; use the default import.

Custom search params on worker imports and new Worker(new URL("./w.js?foo=1", import.meta.url)) URLs are now kept next to Vite's own query (?worker, ?url, ?inline are still stripped); before, user-provided params were dropped from the worker URL.

In builds, inline <style> tags in HTML entries are now minified when build.cssMinify is on (the default) and closing </style> sequences inside them are escaped; before, inline style content was emitted as written.
In builds, a worker chunk is no longer emitted when Vite detects that the code referencing it was removed as unused; before, the worker file was still written to the output.

Asset, CSS, wasm and worker URLs in transformed JS are now emitted as import.meta.ROLLDOWN_FILE_URL_<ref> references resolved by Rolldown (so they honor base and renderBuiltUrl for Rolldown plugins too) instead of Vite's __VITE_ASSET__ placeholders, which changes the intermediate code later plugins see.
Vitest now requires Node.js ^22.12.0 || ^24 || >=26 and Vite >=6.4.0 (Vitest 4 supported Node 20 and Vite 6.0)
vite is no longer a direct dependency of vitest, only a required peer dependency, so it must be installed by the project (package managers that skip peers, such as Yarn, need it in package.json)
clearMocks now defaults to true, so vi.clearAllMocks() runs before every test and mock call history no longer carries over between tests (set clearMocks: false for the old behavior)
testNamePattern / -t now matches the full name joined with ' > ' (as shown in reporters) instead of joining suite and test names with a single space
Inline project configs in test.projects now inherit the root config (extends defaults to true, including Vite plugins and resolve.alias, with arrays merged) instead of inheriting nothing

A config file referenced in test.projects that itself declares projects now contributes those nested projects instead of having its projects field silently ignored; projects is also removed from the inline ProjectConfig type

Inline projects that don't change Vite options now share the declaring config's Vite server (new sharedViteServer option, default true), so that config file and its plugins run once instead of once per project
vi.mock, vi.unmock and vi.hoisted called anywhere but the module top level (inside a function, block or describe/test callback) now throw instead of only logging a warning
In browser mode an automocked module (vi.mock without a factory) now returns auto-generated stubs (undefined) instead of still calling the real implementation

Instances of a class mock (vi.fn(Class), vi.spyOn on a class, mockImplementation(class ...)) now inherit the implementation's prototype methods and pass instanceof the original class; before, prototype methods were undefined on instances
bench is no longer a top-level export of vitest (nor bench.skip/only/todo); benchmarks use the bench fixture from the test context inside a regular test(), with await bench(name, fn).run()

benchmark.reporters, benchmark.outputFile, benchmark.compare, benchmark.outputJson and the --compare and --outputJson CLI flags are removed; benchmark output goes through the default and json reporters and baselines use writeResult/bench.from()
The Vitest instance's mode property is now always 'test'; the 'benchmark' value is no longer used
Vitest UI (and its API and coverage report pages) now require token authentication: /__vitest__/ errors until opened once with the ?token=... URL Vitest prints

vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.setSystemTime() (even without fake timers) now also fake Temporal when it is on the global object, so Temporal.Now follows the mocked clock instead of the real time; opt out with toNotFake: ['Temporal']
toThrow('') / toThrowError('') now matches any error message (substring semantics) instead of only an error with an empty message

Assertion and Matchers types now take the matcher return type first (Assertion<R, T>, Matchers<R, T>), so Assertion<string> becomes Assertion<void, string> and custom matcher declarations must be updated
Vitest no longer picks up custom matcher type declarations from the global jest.Matchers interface; they must augment vitest's Matchers
expect.poll now rejects when the callback or the polled assertion does not settle within timeout, instead of succeeding on a late result; the callback receives an AbortSignal
Unawaited asynchronous assertions (resolves, rejects, toMatchFileSnapshot) now fail the test instead of being auto-awaited at the end with a warning

Inspected values (assertion messages, test.each/test.for title interpolation) are now formatted with pretty-format instead of loupe, changing their rendering; title value truncation is controlled by the new taskTitleValueFormatTruncate option (default 40)
String values interpolated into test.each/test.for titles through a $ placeholder are no longer wrapped in quotes (case 'a1' becomes case a1)
test.sequential, describe.sequential and the sequential test option are removed (deprecated in 4.1); use { concurrent: false }
Locators passed to custom browser commands arrive as a SerializedLocator object ({ selector, locator }) instead of a bare selector string
browser.locators.exact now defaults to true, so text locators such as getByText require a full, case-sensitive match instead of a substring match
Browser-mode toHaveTextContent now requires the element's text to equal the string exactly and no longer accepts a RegExp; the old partial/regex matching moved to the new toMatchTextContent
Glob-pattern coverage thresholds no longer inherit the top-level thresholds.perFile setting; each glob must set perFile itself

coverage.include/exclude globs are now matched against paths relative to the project root without picomatch's contains option, and a pattern without wildcards matches a directory, so they match fewer files than before
Vitest no longer searches parent directories for a config file when run from a subdirectory; pass --config explicitly
In jsdom and happy-dom environments, assignments to globalThis/window properties (such as innerWidth) are now applied to the underlying DOM window instead of only shadowing it on the Node global
populateGlobal's returned originals map now holds property descriptors instead of plain values, so custom environments must restore them with Object.defineProperty
The browser orchestrator page is no longer served from a bare /__vitest_test__/ URL; it requires the sessionId query parameter Vitest generates
browser.api is deprecated and no longer has any effect; browser mode uses the top-level api option (default port still 63315)
The already deprecated browser.isolate option now prints a deprecation warning at startup (its value is still applied to top-level isolate)

Default artifact locations move under .vitest/: attachmentsDir (.vitest-attachements/ to .vitest/attachments/), browser failure screenshots (__screenshots__/ to .vitest/attachments/failure-screenshots/), blob reporter and --merge-reports (.vitest-reports/ to .vitest/blob/), html reporter (html/index.html to .vitest/index.html)
The json and junit reporters now write to .vitest/json/output.json and .vitest/junit/output.xml by default instead of printing to stdout (opt back in with the reporter's stdout option)
The html reporter's output option changed from outputFile (a file path) to outputDir (a directory)
toMatchScreenshot reference screenshots no longer follow browser.screenshotDirectory; they use the new browser.expect.toMatchScreenshot.screenshotDirectory option (default __screenshots__)
VITEST_POOL_ID, VITEST_WORKER_ID and TestModule diagnostic workerId now start at 1 instead of 0
resolveConfig from vitest/node no longer returns { vitestConfig, viteConfig }; it returns the resolved Vite config with the Vitest config on its test property, without creating a server
@vitest/runner (now inlined into vitest and no longer published with it) and @vitest/ws-client are deprecated packages

vitest no longer depends on @vitest/expect; its assertion code is bundled, so the standalone @vitest/expect package no longer shares state with Vitest's expect (use expect, expect.extend and chai from vitest)
@vitest/browser-webdriverio is no longer maintained in the Vitest repo; WebdriverIO support moved to a community package

The entry points deprecated in 4.1 are removed: vitest/coverage and vitest/reporters (use vitest/node), vitest/environments and vitest/snapshot (use vitest/runtime), vitest/runners and vitest/suite (use TestRunner from vitest), plus vitest/mocker and vitest/internal/module-runner
Browser mode no longer scales the tester iframe down to fit the UI, so page.screenshot and toMatchScreenshot capture at the configured viewport resolution
attachmentsDir is now a root-only option: every project writes attachments into the root config's directory and a per-project attachmentsDir is no longer used
vitest list and vitest.collect() now collect tests by static analysis by default instead of running the test files (pass --no-static-parse / staticParse: false for the old behavior)
experimental.fsModuleCache and experimental.fsModuleCachePath are deprecated (migrated with a warning) in favor of the top-level fsModuleCache and fsModuleCachePath options
The Vitest instance methods experimental_parseSpecifications and experimental_clearCache are deprecated aliases that log a warning; use parseSpecifications and clearCache
Setting deps.optimizer.web (the Vitest 3 alias for client, already ignored) now logs a deprecation warning pointing to deps.optimizer.client, unless a Vite environment named web exists
fsModuleCache is now enabled by default, so transformed modules are persisted on disk across runs (disable with fsModuleCache: false)

Browser mode now treats each browser instance as a worker: at most maxWorkers instances/pages are open at once across projects, so fewer browsers open by default than the previous projects x maxWorkers
z.iso.datetime() (with or without offset: true) rejects minute-precision input such as 2020-01-01T06:15Z that it accepted before; local: true still allows it.
String .min()/.max()/.length() count Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so astral characters such as emoji count once.
A record's key schema governs only keys that match it, so intersecting an object with a pattern-keyed record no longer rejects the object's own keys as invalid_key.
An unrecognized_keys issue no longer aborts the object it came from, so a strict object with an extra key and a bad value reports both issues instead of the first alone.
Object and record parsers always drop a __proto__ key (from input, schema or key transform), and .strict() reports an own __proto__ input key as unrecognized_keys instead of swallowing it.

Several string formats are stricter: z.ipv6() checks the address alphabet directly instead of via new URL() (rejecting ::1 followed by a newline), z.ulid() requires a first character of 0-7, z.httpUrl() enforces the RFC 1035 host length limits, the z.emoji() regex no longer backtracks exponentially, and the JSON Schema pattern for .includes(sub, { position: N }) allows at least N leading characters instead of exactly N.

ZodNumberFormat takes a format type parameter so ZodInt, ZodFloat32, ZodFloat64, ZodInt32 and ZodUInt32 (and the bigint formats) are distinct at the type level instead of one interchangeable type (commit marked with !).
The ZodError produced by .safeParse() no longer captures a stack trace at construction, so result.error.stack is not the call site it used to be.

z.toJSONSchema() behaves differently for inputs it already handled: a root schema with an id in its metadata is emitted as a root $ref into $defs, a union of simple primitive types becomes a type array instead of anyOf, and the override callback runs before the unrepresentable error is thrown.
.safeParse() builds its ZodError lazily, so error maps (global, locale and per-schema error) run when result.error is first read rather than at parse time.
z.emoji() rejects strings made only of emoji components (digits, #, *, lone modifiers or joiners) such as "123" that it previously accepted.
z.enum(NumericEnum).options lists only the numeric values; the reverse-mapping member names that it used to include (and that failed to parse) are gone.

The runtime regexes behind z.base64()/z.base64url() check only the alphabet with length and padding enforced in code (z.regexes.base64url becomes the length-aware form), and the z.email() pattern (z.regexes.email, issue.pattern and the JSON Schema pattern) drops its lookaheads and capture groups; composing either into a template literal no longer applies the dropped rules to the rest of the string.
z.toJSONSchema() folds chained checks as a conjunction, so a later format check no longer overwrites tighter min/max bounds and repeated multipleOf or min/length chains emit the correct constraints.

Schema members .format, .minLength, .maxLength, .minValue, .maxValue, .isInt, .minDate and .maxDate are prototype getters materialized on first read (absent from Object.keys until then) and report the tightest bound rather than the last-written one.

z.fromJSONSchema() turns a positional tuple (prefixItems, or a draft-7 items array) with no additionalItems/items:false into an open-ended tuple that accepts extra elements; before, it built a closed tuple that rejected them.
z.fromJSONSchema() converts format: "hostname" into a z.hostname() check; before, the format was ignored and any string was accepted.

The Zod 3 compat aliases ZodTypeAny, ZodSchema, Schema, TypeOf, Infer, ZodFirstPartySchemaTypes, ZodFlattenedError, ZodFormattedError, ZodErrorMap and the _max/_min helpers now carry a @deprecated tag TypeScript actually reports; before, the tag was lost on re-export and editors showed them as normal.

z.fromJSONSchema() enforces minProperties, maxProperties, uniqueItems, contains, minContains and maxContains; before, it silently dropped them, so the converted schema accepted data the JSON Schema rejects.
